about: A workflow every account can find and run: start and run a faceless slideshow page that sells one small digital product (a cookbook, a plan, a template pack). Pick a niche, keep one visual style, post carousels whose last slide is the product, take payment through a checkout the person sets up, and review every week. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks).

payload.produces: Each Monday: which carousels won on views and saves, the part 2 of each winner, and the video of the biggest one; the before-and-after numbers are a weekly results post.
payload.label: Run a slideshow page that sells a small digital product
payload.job: Build a slideshow page around the person's own material and one small paid product: list the material they really made, read the biggest pages in the niche for their top 3 formats, fix one visual style, outline the product with every item marked as the person's own or still to make, write a batch of carousels whose first slide names who it is for and whose last slide shows the product with one action, render them as 1080x1350 images, get the person's approval of every batch, schedule only approved posts, and each week read views, saves and sales, make part 2 of the winners and turn the biggest winner into a video. Every number comes from a tool call, a package label, a cited database or the person's own analytics; where there is none, the answer is "no data". The AI drafts and renders; the person approves, owns every account and the checkout, and the AI never posts by itself.

source.author: Three X posts on slideshow pages
source.name: A post of 2026-10-29 on a meal-idea slideshow page that sells a EUR 4.99 cookbook (60 recipes and a 7-day plan) from its last slide, studied from its screen recording; plus Ernesto Lopez on slideshow pages (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2112940887806296269, quoted by https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115442722660037110) and on AI cooking reels (https://x.com/ErnestoSOFTWARE/status/2115897827775988205)
source.note: Their claims, not checked here: the page had 462K likes with under 8K followers (the recording shows that 462K is the profile's lifetime likes; the one post shown had 1,620 likes and 635 saves); one recipe page has 488M views; 5M views brings about $2,000 to $5,000 in revenue; some sounds average about 10 times the page average. The observed format: six slides (a cover, then breakfast, lunch, dinner and dessert, one per slide, then the product), each meal slide a top-down plate, a two-line label naming the slot and three ingredients joined with '+', and three ingredient cut-outs; the last slide is the product mock-up, an outcome headline and one 'link in bio' button; the bio holds one link to a one-screen page with a single price button. The method from the article: a first slide that names who it is for and forces the next swipe; rerun a winning hook as numbered parts; one theme or character on every post; keep a sound that works; the product on the last slide and its full name in the caption; pull the biggest page's posts with views and saves, find its top 3 formats, brief 2 months, generate about 120, a person approves, schedule, and every Monday read views, make a part 2 of the winners and turn the biggest winners into video. His paid tools are replaced with open ones: ViewTrack by yt-dlp and gallery-dl metadata reads, Higgsfield by mflux image generation, Kling and Seedance by mlx-video or ltx-2-mlx, Postiz cloud by self-hosted Postiz (AGPL-3.0), and the Slack AI employee by this workflow on the person's own AI. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) AI-generated food or product photos shown as the person's own work mislead buyers, so generated images are labelled as illustrations and the person's own photos come first; (2) nutrition or health claims beyond a cited label or database are not written, because a recipe product that promises health results makes claims nobody checked; (3) bulk scraping of rival pages breaks platform terms, so rivals are read one public page at a time as metadata only and nothing is downloaded but numbers and links.

niche.description: The page's subject in the person's own words, for example high-protein meals or budget travel

audience.description: Who the page is for, as specifically as the person can say it

kind.description: What the product is, for example a PDF cookbook with a 7-day plan

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, for example EUR or USD

own_material.description: Where the person's own material lives: folder paths, document paths or notes they wrote, one per item

rival_pages.description: Public profile addresses of the biggest pages in the niche, if the person knows them

platform.description: Where the page will post its carousels

batch_size.description: How many carousels to draft in one batch

steps.title: List what the person really made
steps.do: Open every path in the input own_material and read it. List each thing the person actually made, cooked, wrote or photographed, with the exact file path or quote that shows it. For each, copy any amounts and any numbers printed on a package label or written in their notes, with where they came from. List the person's own photos that show the thing, by file path. Do not add anything the material does not show: if you think the person might make something, it does not go in this list.

evidence.description: The file path, and the line or quote, that shows the person made it

checks.says: At least one thing the person really made is listed

steps.title: Read the biggest pages in the niche, numbers only
steps.do: If the input rival_pages is empty, call tool:read-public-web-page on a web search for the niche plus the platform name and copy up to 5 profile addresses of pages that post carousels on it; if none show, send them as an empty list and write "no data". For each profile, read post metadata only: use tool:github:mikf-gallery-dl with `gallery-dl --dump-json --no-download <profile address>` for photo carousels and tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp with `yt-dlp --flat-playlist --dump-json <profile address>` for videos. Read one profile at a time and download no media. From each post copy the address, the post date, view_count and the save or collect count when the tool returns one; when it returns none, write null and add the field name to no_data. Mark a post an outlier when its views are at least 5 times the median views of its own profile. Name the 3 formats the outliers share in plain words, each with its typical first-slide hook, its slide count, how the product appears and the number of outliers it covers (at least 3).

checks.says: Every post comes from a page that was read

steps.title: Fix one visual style for every post
steps.do: Write one style sheet the whole page will use, taken from the person's own photos and material where they exist: slide size 1080x1350 pixels; background colour as a hex value; one typeface for labels and one for accents, both with a licence that allows commercial use (name the licence); the label size in pixels, at least 44; at most 12 words a slide; where the photo sits; and the photo rule: the person's own photos first, a text-led slide when there is no photo, and any generated image labelled "illustration" on the slide. If the page has a recurring character, describe it in one sentence and name the tool that keeps it the same in every image (tool:github:mflux-community-mflux with the same reference image every time).

checks.says: The page never uses stock photos as the person's work

steps.title: Outline the product, marking what is the person's own
steps.do: Write the product's contents as a list of items. Mark each item own (it is in the own-material list, under the same name) or to-make (the person has not made it yet). Never mark an item own unless the own-material step listed it. For every number in the product (amounts, calories, protein, prices), write its source: the package label or note from the own-material step, or a cited database entry (for food, USDA FoodData Central with its FDC id). Write no health claim: describe what a thing contains, never what it does to a body. Write the sales page words in the one-screen shape: what it contains in one line, a headline that names the outcome, one proof line, one price button with the input price, and the payment and delivery terms in one line.

own_items.description: The names of the items marked own

checks.says: An item is marked own only when the person's own material shows it
No health or result promise in the headline
No health or result promise in the proof line

steps.title: Write the batch of carousels slide by slide
steps.do: Write as many carousels as the input batch_size, each in one of the formats from the rivals step, keeping the format's structure and writing every word new. Slide 1 names exactly who it is for and makes the next swipe necessary. Middle slides follow the style sheet: one item each, the item's name and what you need, at most the style sheet's words per slide, using only items from the product outline. The last slide shows the product and one action ("link in bio"), with no price. Give each carousel a series name and a part number, so a hook that wins can come back as part 2. Write the caption with the product's full name. Name the photo for every slide: the person's photo path, "text only", or "illustration" with the generation prompt.

checks.says: Every carousel uses a format found in the rivals step
Carousels show only items from the product outline
No health or result promise in a hook

steps.title: Render every slide as a 1080x1350 image
steps.do: For each slide write one HTML file that follows the style sheet exactly (size, background, fonts, label size, photo position), embedding the slide's own photo by its file path, or no photo for a text-only slide, or the generated image for an illustration with the word "illustration" printed on the slide. For an illustration, generate the image with tool:github:mflux-community-mflux on the person's computer, using the same reference image for every slide of a recurring character. Open each HTML file in a headless Chromium (Playwright) with a 1080 by 1350 viewport and save a PNG screenshot next to it. Look at every PNG: no text cut off, nothing overlapping, the words match the script exactly.

checks.says: Every image belongs to a written carousel

steps.title: The person approves every carousel exactly as rendered
steps.do: Show the person, in the chat, every rendered image of each carousel in order, with its caption and the source of every number on it. Ask for each carousel: "Do you approve this carousel exactly as shown?" Wait. If they change anything, make only that change, render again and ask again. Copy their approving answer exactly into approval_words. Nothing is posted or scheduled in this step, and no carousel goes further without its own approval.

approval_words.description: The person's own words approving this exact carousel

checks.says: Each approved carousel is a drafted carousel, unchanged

steps.title: The person sets up the product page and checkout
steps.do: Call tool:tell-the-person with { "title": "Set up the checkout for your product", "body": "Create the product page and checkout in your own account with a payment provider you choose, using the page words I drafted, and send me its address. I do not create accounts or take payments for you." } and include the page words from the product step. Wait for the address. Then call tool:make-tracked-link with the checkout address so visits from the page can be counted, and give the person the tracked link to put in the profile bio as the one link.

steps.title: Schedule only the approved carousels
steps.do: Use the person's own self-hosted Postiz (tool:github:gitroomhq-postiz-app) with the platform account the person connected to it; if they have none, give them each approved carousel's images and caption with its date and time, and they post it by hand. Schedule one or two carousels a day, only from the approved list, each with its caption unchanged. Copy each scheduled time.

steps.title: Every Monday: read the numbers, make part 2 of the winners
steps.do: Every Monday, read each posted carousel's views and saves with tool:github:mikf-gallery-dl or tool:github:yt-dlp-yt-dlp metadata from the person's own profile, and the week's visits and sales with tool:break-down-visits-and-sales for the tracked link. Mark a carousel a winner when its views are at least 2 times the page's median for the last 4 weeks. For each winner write the brief for its next part (same hook, same series, new items from the product outline). For the single biggest winner, write a video brief and make it on the person's computer with tool:github:blaizzy-mlx-video from the approved slides, labelled as generated where it shows generated food. Then go back to the carousels step with these briefs; every new carousel and video passes the approve step again.

sales.description: Sales counted for the tracked link this week, or null with the reason in no_data

checks.says: Numbers are read only for posts that were scheduled
Winners come from the posts read this week
